title: I, Rooted in the World
statement: A self is never singular in isolation. Here the “I” appears as a body held between Earth and the city, history and growth: Frederick Douglass anchors the image while a botanical crown and leaf extend identity beyond the skin. The distant planet turns private presence into a shared condition.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make an image of what the word “I” means when you use it.

notes.note: Build a layered self-portrait: Earth and lunar ground as the existential field, Frederick Douglass as the central embodied “I,” with botanical growth and a vertical city axis suggesting identity rooted between nature, history, and society.

Here the “I” appears as a body held between Earth and the city, history and growth: Frederick Douglass anchors the image while a botanical crown and leaf extend identity beyond the skin. notes.note: The central figure reads clearly, but the city strip currently dominates the face and the botanical crown floats too far above the head. I will tighten the vertical identity axis, integrate the crown with the portrait, and add a red flamingo as a contrasting outward gesture while keeping the lunar field as the ground.

The latest canvas has a strong solitary figure against Earthrise, but the intended civic axis is hidden and the composition has too much empty black around the subject. I will reveal the Flatiron as a visible vertical “I” over the portrait and add a low band of collective human activity to ground the individual socially.
notes.error: Layer index must be an integer from 0 to 5.

notes.note: The canvas now reads as a solitary human presence in cosmic space, with botanical growth and the flamingo creating a vivid outward “I.” The city piece is hidden beneath the portrait, so I will bring it forward as a narrow civic spine and add the crowd as a grounded social horizon without disturbing the central figure.

The inspected canvas is finished: the portrait is the unmistakable central “I,” the narrow Flatiron fragment forms a literal inner vertical, and the surrounding flower, flamingo, crowd, and Earthrise expand the self into growth, expression, society, and shared world. The title and statement are present and nonblank.
